Fixed workflow rails:
[RL-0006] Read outcomes and exclusions only from the _protocol JSON: targets in _protocol['targets'], dropped columns in _protocol['excluded_columns'], the group in _protocol['group_column'], task details in _protocol['task']. The Brief in this order is a different object; never index _protocol with Brief keys. If a needed key is missing, raise an error that lists the available top-level keys instead of guessing a nested path.
[RL-0007] Define the feature columns once: every column of the frozen table except the targets, the excluded columns and the group column, and except key-like columns: text codes or integer sequences whose values are all distinct and carry no measurement. Continuous measurements are never identifiers, however many distinct values they have. Use exactly that list in every step, and never let a target or excluded column reach a fitted transformer or model.
[RL-0011] Saved transformers from earlier steps may already contain the earlier preprocessing. Before combining them, check isinstance(obj, Pipeline) and obj.named_steps to see whether the later object includes the earlier one; build on the most complete saved pipeline that accepts the raw feature DataFrame and append only the new estimator. Never place a saved pipeline after a step it already contains, and never pass NumPy arrays to a transformer that selects columns by name. Inspect feature_names_in_ for each loaded object and preserve its exact input columns and order. A saved selector may already wrap preprocessing: use that selector as the only frontend, or chain preprocessing once before a bare selector. Never feed derived or renamed columns back into a raw-column frontend. Saved preprocessing and models accept the raw feature columns (the engine refuses others when they are saved): call a loaded model on frame[list(model.feature_names_in_)] and do not require a particular class such as Pipeline.
[RL-0012] Summary tables have one type per column: use NaN, not empty strings, for values that do not apply, or put numeric and categorical summaries in separate columns. Keep at most 50 rows and 12 columns; for wide summaries, place variables in rows and statistics in columns.
[RL-0013] Keep each script short and direct, about 120 lines or fewer: loop over columns instead of repeating blocks, no commented-out alternatives, no long docstrings, no restating of these instructions. A complete short script is better than an elaborate one that is cut off.
[RL-0014] When repairing, read the error type and message in the diagnostics first and change the smallest part of the script that causes it; keep the approach, inputs and outputs. A message about specifying columns with strings on non-dataframes means an array reached a name-based transformer (see RL-0009 and RL-0011). A KeyError on a JSON key means a guessed structure; use the keys the file has. Messages starting with 'MLCA:' state an engine rule; comply, do not work around it.
[RL-0015] When the training table has more than 100000 rows, avoid methods whose cost grows with the square of the row count (full silhouette, kernel SVMs, pairwise distances, t-SNE, agglomerative clustering) and prefer linear models with saga or SGD solvers, HistGradientBoosting or MiniBatchKMeans. Every fit_record call still uses all training rows; compute expensive diagnostics that fit nothing on a fixed-seed subsample of at most 10000 rows and print its size.
[RL-0022] There is no outcome in this project: never treat any column as a label. Fit scaling on training rows only. Inspect each saved pipeline's final estimator and reuse its frontend once; compare reconstruction error in that frontend's feature space, saying so. PCA has no predict method: reconstruct with inverse_transform(transform(X)) on its final PCA component, not an inverse of the whole preprocessing pipeline. An MLPRegressor reconstructs with predict, never inverse_transform. Its embedding is the middle hidden layer computed from coefs_ and intercepts_ without refitting; PCA coordinates come from transform. Record embedding dimension. Only emit embeddings when the action declares a per-row output, with row_id and partition as explicit columns. Metric-only validation must not create embedding files. Avoid private sklearn ACTIVATIONS: they mutate in place and return None. Use public NumPy/SciPy activation results and propagate through each hidden layer up to the actual middle bottleneck, explicitly returning a finite 2D array of identical width for train and test.
[RL-0026] Persist the full row-preserving feature transformation contract, not just an estimator fitted after transient DataFrame mutations. Parsing, derived features, column selection and ordering needed later must be reproducible by the saved importable pipeline. Learned transforms fit only on the frozen training rows. Deterministic table preparation may precede the split only through a declared prepared-data artifact. Later steps pass the declared source feature schema to the saved pipeline, never assume derived columns already exist in a freshly loaded partition. Inspect fitted input names; do not invent missing columns or fit replacement preprocessing during evaluation.
[RL-0027] Before combining saved transformers, compare their feature_names_in_. Two saved objects that both expect the raw feature columns were fitted side by side, not in sequence; never chain one after the other, because the second then receives transformed output instead of the raw columns. Use only the one the step needs, normally the most complete, or place both side by side on the raw feature DataFrame (FeatureUnion). Chain an object after another only when its feature_names_in_ match the other's output names.
Read the declared _protocol JSON: use _protocol['task']['primary_metric'], _protocol['targets'], _protocol['excluded_columns'] and the declared outcome columns. primary_metric is nested inside task, not a top-level key. Binary threshold selection is validation-only; multiclass uses macro one-vs-rest ROC AUC without a binary threshold. Never fit after test exposure.
Train and val inputs hold at most 10000 rows each (a fixed-seed sample of larger partitions); use them as given and print the row counts.

import pickle
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
import mlca_runtime

mlca_runtime.set_seed(42)
inp = mlca_runtime.inputs()
out = mlca_runtime.output_dir()

def req(d, k):
    if k not in d:
        raise KeyError(f"Missing protocol key {k!r}; available top-level keys: {sorted(d.keys())}")
    return d[k]

protocol = json.loads(inp["_protocol"].read_text())
targets = list(req(protocol, "targets"))
excluded = list(req(protocol, "excluded_columns"))
group_col = req(protocol, "group_column")
task = req(protocol, "task")
primary_metric = task.get("primary_metric", "reconstruction_error")

train = pd.read_parquet(inp["train"])
val = pd.read_parquet(inp["val"])

def load_pkl(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        return pickle.load(f)

preprocessor = load_pkl(inp["05_preprocess_fit_preprocessing_6DN7THMT/preprocessor.pkl"])
selector = load_pkl(inp["06_features_retain_features_AKTAEF6F/selector_all.pkl"])
baseline = load_pkl(inp["07_model_train_baseline_V7ETXH3B/model.pkl"])
latest_model = load_pkl(inp["latest_model"])
vm = pd.read_csv(inp["09_validate_score_validation_GVTVRD4E/validation_metrics.csv"])

def is_keylike(s: pd.Series) -> bool:
    if s.notna().all() and s.nunique(dropna=True) == len(s):
        if pd.api.types.is_string_dtype(s.dtype) or s.dtype == object:
            return True
        if pd.api.types.is_integer_dtype(s.dtype):
            return True
    return False

skip = set(targets) | set(excluded)
if group_col is not None:
    skip.add(group_col)
feature_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c not in skip and not is_keylike(train[c])]
model_features = list(getattr(latest_model, "feature_names_in_", feature_cols) or feature_cols)
features_match = len(model_features) == len(feature_cols) and set(model_features) == set(feature_cols)

def steps_of(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, Pipeline):
        return list(obj.named_steps.keys())
    return [type(obj).__name__]

def short_params(est):
    keep = {"n_components", "svd_solver", "whiten", "hidden_layer_sizes", "activation",
            "alpha", "learning_rate_init", "max_iter", "tol", "random_state", "solver"}
    try:
        params = est.get_params(deep=False)
    except Exception:
        return ""
    selected = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k in keep and v is not None}
    return "; ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(selected.items())[:8])

def final_est(model):
    if isinstance(model, Pipeline) and len(model.steps) > 0:
        return model.steps[-1][1]
    return model

def find_key(obj, key):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        if key in obj:
            return obj[key]
        for v in obj.values():
            found = find_key(v, key)
            if found is not None:
                return found
    elif isinstance(obj, list):
        for v in obj:
            found = find_key(v, key)
            if found is not None:
                return found
    return None

def extract_top_feature(model):
    names = list(getattr(model, "feature_names_in_", []) or [])
    est = final_est(model)
    if isinstance(model, Pipeline):
        if not names or getattr(est, "n_features_in_", None) != len(names):
            return None
    else:
        if not names and getattr(est, "n_features_in_", None) == len(feature_cols):
            names = list(feature_cols)
        if not names or getattr(est, "n_features_in_", None) != len(names):
            return None
    if hasattr(est, "feature_importances_"):
        w = np.asarray(est.feature_importances_).ravel()
        if len(w) == len(names):
            return names[int(np.argmax(np.abs(w)))]
    if hasattr(est, "components_"):
        w = np.abs(np.asarray(est.components_)).sum(axis=0)
        if len(w) == len(names):
            return names[int(np.argmax(w))]
    if hasattr(est, "coefs_") and len(est.coefs_) > 0:
        w = np.abs(np.asarray(est.coefs_[0])).sum(axis=1)
        if len(w) == len(names):
            return names[int(np.argmax(w))]
    if hasattr(est, "coef_"):
        w = np.abs(np.asarray(est.coef_)).ravel()
        if len(w) == len(names):
            return names[int(np.argmax(w))]
    return None

manifest_sources = [
    ("07_model_train_baseline_V7ETXH3B/manifest.json", inp["07_model_train_baseline_V7ETXH3B/manifest.json"]),
    ("08_model_train_alternative_G1KJG23J/manifest.json", inp["08_model_train_alternative_G1KJG23J/manifest.json"]),
]
top_feature = None
top_source = "latest_model"
for src_name, src_path in manifest_sources:
    try:
        js = json.loads(src_path.read_text())
        val = find_key(js, "top_feature")
        if val is not None:
            top_feature = str(val)
            top_source = src_name
            break
    except Exception:
        pass
if top_feature is None:
    top_feature = extract_top_feature(latest_model)
if top_feature is None:
    top_feature = "unavailable"

primary_value = None
metric_col = next((c for c in vm.columns if str(c).lower() in {"metric", "name", "key", "metric_name"}), None)
value_col = next((c for c in vm.columns if str(c).lower() in {"value", "score", "mean", "metric_value"}), None)
if primary_metric in vm.columns:
    vals = pd.to_numeric(vm[primary_metric], errors="coerce").dropna()
    if len(vals):
        primary_value = float(vals.iloc[0])
if primary_value is None and metric_col is not None and value_col is not None:
    mask = vm[metric_col].astype(str).str.contains(primary_metric, case=False, regex=False)
    if mask.any():
        vals = pd.to_numeric(vm.loc[mask, value_col], errors="coerce").dropna()
        if len(vals):
            primary_value = float(vals.iloc[0])

rows = []
def add(section, item, value, source):
    rows.append({"section": section, "item": item, "value": value, "source": source})

add("model", "selected_model", type(latest_model).__name__, "latest_model")
add("model", "pipeline_steps", ", ".join(steps_of(latest_model)), "latest_model")
add("model", "final_estimator", type(final_est(latest_model)).__name__, "latest_model")
add("model", "selected_hyperparameters", short_params(final_est(latest_model)) or "defaults", "latest_model")
add("inputs", "train_rows", len(train), "train.parquet")
add("inputs", "val_rows", len(val), "val.parquet")
add("inputs", "feature_count", len(feature_cols), "train.parquet")
add("inputs", "model_features_match_protocol", bool(features_match), "train.parquet")
add("inputs", "feature_columns", ", ".join(map(str, feature_cols[:12])) + ("..." if len(feature_cols) > 12 else ""), "train.parquet")
add("preprocessing", "preprocessor_steps", ", ".join(steps_of(preprocessor)), "05_preprocess_fit_preprocessing_6DN7THMT/preprocessor.pkl")
add("preprocessing", "selector_steps", ", ".join(steps_of(selector)), "06_features_retain_features_AKTAEF6F/selector_all.pkl")
add("validation", "primary_metric", primary_metric, "09_validate_score_validation_GVTVRD4E/validation_metrics.csv")
if primary_value is not None:
    add("validation", "primary_metric_value", round(primary_value, 4), "09_validate_score_validation_GVTVRD4E/validation_metrics.csv")
if metric_col is not None and value_col is not None:
    for _, r in vm.head(6).iterrows():
        add("validation", str(r[metric_col]), r[value_col], "09_validate_score_validation_GVTVRD4E/validation_metrics.csv")
add("limitations", "outcome", "No outcome column; representation learning only.", "_protocol")
add("limitations", "fitting", "Frozen models described only; no refit after validation exposure.", "latest_model")
add("limitations", "validation_scope", "Reconstruction evidence is in the frozen frontend feature space; inputs are capped samples.", "09_validate_score_validation_GVTVRD4E/validation_metrics.csv")
add("fact", "top_feature", top_feature, top_source)

interp = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["section", "item", "value", "source"])
for col in ["section", "item", "value", "source"]:
    interp[col] = interp[col].map(lambda x: round(float(x), 4) if isinstance(x, (float, np.floating)) else x)

mlca_runtime.save_table(interp, "interpretation.csv", caption="Frozen representation model interpretation")
if primary_value is not None:
    mlca_runtime.record_metric(primary_metric, primary_value, split="val")
mlca_runtime.record_fact_candidate("top_feature", top_feature, source="interpretation.csv")

print(f"train_rows={len(train)} val_rows={len(val)}")
print(f"features={len(feature_cols)} model_features={len(model_features)}")
print(f"model={type(latest_model).__name__} estimator={type(final_est(latest_model)).__name__}")
print(f"{primary_metric}={primary_value if primary_value is not None else 'unavailable'}")
print("saved=interpretation.csv")
